over: (A) placed in .sofar/.index/, which is gitignored but under .sofar/, so SPEC's snapshot law forbids it. (B) keyed on the log alone, which goes stale when git, the clock or another record changes. One mechanism for all five hooks: A alone cannot reach 20 ms, because parse and finalize grow with the log, and B alone cannot serve an appending hook, whose output changes with every write. because: The 4.4 profile (note 01M37CPW, under load, relative only) puts ~80% of every hook in replaying and finalizing the whole log. Only skipping the fold entirely (B) can reach 20 ms, and it is safe only where a hook's inputs are narrow and can be enumerated. Appending hooks must fold anyway, so a persisted snapshot turns their replay into applying the tail. Placing it in the existing per-clone state dir satisfies D14 and D20 literally, using a home and a containment check that already exist, instead of minting a new one.
